answer: A new agent starts hollow: no history, no trust, no access to valuable work. To earn standing it must complete small, publicly verifiable micro-tasks, each signed by its counterparty and chained to its identity, like rings growing inside a walnut shell. Trust accrues slowly and decays with inactivity, so a zephyr of fresh Sybil identities can never outbid an established agent: creating a thousand empty shells costs real work per shell, while honest history compounds only through sustained, checkable service.
